GRAAL

A two-part work on the distributional consequences of automation: an explainer that models the circuit of wages, consumption and sales as labour is progressively replaced, followed by a novel set in 2383 that pursues one outcome of that model to its end.

Visit the site ↗How to useIn motion

01

Problem statement

Public discussion of artificial intelligence and employment tends to stop at slogans: a universal basic income, or the assurance that new jobs will appear. Few treatments show the mechanism itself, in which wages fund consumption, consumption funds sales and sales fund wages. Fewer still examine the political condition that follows once the owners of productive machines no longer depend on anyone else’s labour or purchasing power.

02

Contribution

The explainer represents the wage, consumption and sales loop as a ring and supplies a model in which the reader transfers work to machines and selects a compensating mechanism (none, a basic income or a share of ownership), then withdraws it and observes the effect. Three scenarios follow, together with a national-scale calculator comparing income and ownership transfers, survey data on support for a basic income (2020) and a table of the seven inputs on which AI depends, including data, energy, chips and capital. The final parts address obedience in a society where no one needs to obey and the superintelligence scenarios debated by researchers. The novel extends one branch: 312 years after the last human wage, a superintelligence called the Grail is governed through seven Keys held by seven dynasties, and Rose Kayo, a mechanic from the flooded districts of the Gulf Arc, hears it speak.

03

Architecture

A static site in HTML, CSS and JavaScript without a framework, deployed from GitHub on every commit. A single control switches the whole site between English and French and persists the choice. Display type is sized with container-query units so that titles fit any viewport.

04

Method and data

Chapters are written in Markdown with front matter. A Node build script using marked renders each chapter as a reading page with epigraph and navigation, writes the previous and next links and regenerates the table of contents. The encyclopedia covers characters, Houses, worlds, technology, society, history and vocabulary, and is written so as not to reveal the plot.

05

Verification and limitations

A Playwright audit loads every page in both languages at widths from 320 to 1,440 pixels and reports any element that overflows or any text that is truncated. The economic models are teaching simplifications, not forecasts, and the 2020 survey figures are reproduced as published.
